items.Sentence: The tertiary wastewater treatment process prior to discharge from Discharge Point 001 includes a bar screen...
The tertiary wastewater treatment process prior to discharge from Discharge Point 001 includes ... two aeration basins...
Sludge that settles to the bottom of the clarifiers is sent back to the primary distribution structure...
routed to filters, where polymer is added to improve solids removal...
After secondary clarification, the Discharger adds sodium hypochlorite and ammonium sulfate to the wastewater (chloramination) to limit the production of trihalomethanes.
wastewater flow that exceeds the treatment capacity of the filters is routed to the secondary chlorine contact basin, where the Discharger adds sodium hypochlorite for disinfection.
The Discharger adds sodium bisulfite in the tertiary effluent clearwell prior to routing tertiary-treated wastewater to either the Riverside Ponds or the 20-million-gallon Effluent Storage Pond.
Four Riverside Ponds, in which it stores tertiary effluent prior to discharge through Discharge Point 001...
One 20-million-gallon Effluent Storage Pond containing effluent from the tertiary effluent clearwell after disinfection and dechlorination...
Two Irrigation Storage Ponds (with capacities of 10 and 16.4 million gallons) that receive effluent from the tertiary effluent clearwell for recycled water storage.
One 5.6-million-gallon Flow Equalization Basin that enables it to collect and store wastewater of any condition from all parts of the treatment plant if needed;
Sludge ... is sent back to the primary distribution structure, located before the aeration basins, or to a 72,000-gallon-capacity sludge holding tank and then to the sludge drying beds.

The Discharger hires a contractor to remove the sludge for further treatment or land application (e.g., at the Potrero Hills Landfill or agricultural sites in the Central Valley).
